sources.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997)
sources.locator: Chapter 1, §§1.2–1.3, PDF pp. 30–31 (printed pp. 23–24); Chapter 6, §§6.1–6.2, PDF pp. 149–153 (printed pp. 142–146), including equations (6.10)–(6.14); Chapter 7, equations (7.106)–(7.113), PDF pp. 208–210 (printed pp. 201–203). Complete relevant sections inspected.

contents.name: Chapter 1: Hodge star and Maxwell equations in differential-form notation
contents.support: The source fixes the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention and differential-form Maxwell equations; the varied Hodge formula is derived in the local lemma.

contents.name: Chapter 6: Linearized metric perturbations and infinitesimal diffeomorphism gauge transformations
contents.support: The source motivates the perturbation and gauge conventions; the curved-background naturality argument is proved locally rather than imported from its flat-background formulas.

contents.name: Chapter 7: Reissner–Nordström field, charge parameter and exterior solution
contents.support: The RN field and charge normalization match the geometric supplier; the example computes its flux variation on one fixed exterior chart.

sources.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020)
sources.locator: Section 1, PDF pp. 1–4, and §§6.1–6.2, PDF pp. 43–55; complete relevant sections inspected, including the coupled perturbation model, pure-gauge modes, parameter modes, and the distinct hypotheses of the global decay theorem.

contents.name: §1: Coupled linearized Einstein–Maxwell model and theorem hypotheses
contents.support: Supports the coupled perturbation context. The local definition explicitly avoids importing the paper’s small-charge asymptotically flat decay theorem or its gauge normalization.

contents.name: §6.1: Pure-gauge linearized solutions
contents.support: Supports the pure-gauge mode context; the local proof derives the claim from tensorial naturality.

contents.name: §6.2: Linearized Kerr–Newman parameter modes
contents.support: Supports the existence of parameter modes; the local proof differentiates exact families on common domains and does not classify the full kernel.

sources.title: Helmut Friedrich and Alan Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1, arXiv:gr-qc/0002074
sources.locator: Section 3.1, PDF pp. 22–31; the complete section inspected for symmetric first-order systems, integration-by-parts energy identities, commutator estimates, and the distinction between a local estimate and existence or continuation.

contents.name: §3.1: Symmetric first-order systems and local energy identity
contents.support: Supports the energy method. The local proof supplies its own coefficient commutator bound, finite-slab source term and exact Maxwell and harmonic subsidiary identities.

contents.name: §3.1: Higher-order commutator estimates and local-versus-global scope
contents.support: The source distinguishes local energy control from existence, continuation and global decay; the carrier preserves those limitations and makes no global stability claim.

sources.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997)
sources.locator: Chapter 1, §§1.2–1.3, PDF pp. 30–31 (printed pp. 23–24), and Chapter 7, equations (7.106)–(7.113), PDF pp. 208–210 (printed pp. 201–203); complete relevant sections inspected.

contents.name: Chapter 1: Oriented Lorentzian Hodge formula
contents.support: The local verification uses the source’s Hodge convention and computes the RN electric flux, with the outward orientation fixed by the RN data supplier.

contents.name: Chapter 7: Exact Reissner–Nordström electric-charge family
contents.support: The family is fixed on a common exterior domain; its stationarity, linearization and nonzero flux variation are verified directly.

sources.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020)
sources.locator: §6.2, PDF pp. 51–55; complete section inspected for the linearized Kerr–Newman parameter family and the pure parameter modes.

contents.name: §6.2: Non-radiating parameter derivatives in the Kerr–Newman family
contents.support: Supports the parameter-mode motivation; the local RN example independently computes one charge derivative and does not rely on the paper’s decay theorem.

contents.name: §6.2: Gauge normalization and distinction from radiative decay claims
contents.support: The example is limited to a stationary exact-family derivative and makes no universal decay or physical-observation claim.
